differential.name: Diabetic nephropathy (stage 4 chronic kidney disease with nephrotic-range proteinuria)

supporting_evidence.finding: Stage 4 CKD with eGFR ~20 mL/min/1.73 m²
Long‑standing type 2 diabetes mellitus, poor glycemic control (HbA1c >8%)

differential.reasoning: The combination of advanced diabetic disease, markedly reduced eGFR, and nephrotic‑range proteinuria is classic for diabetic kidney disease and accounts for the majority of the renal dysfunction.

differential.name: Atherosclerotic coronary artery disease with prior coronary artery bypass graft (CABG)

supporting_evidence.finding: History of CABG performed 5 years ago
Age >70 y with multiple vascular risk factors

differential.reasoning: Prior revascularization and persistent risk factors make recurrent or progressive coronary artery disease highly likely, contributing to overall morbidity.

differential.name: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF)

supporting_evidence.finding: Clinical history of dyspnea on exertion, peripheral edema
Risk factors: hypertension, CAD, CKD, obesity

differential.reasoning: Symptoms and risk profile are compatible with HFpEF, though confirmation requires echocardiography and natriuretic peptide levels, which are currently missing.

differential.name: CKD‑related anemia of chronic disease / erythropoietin deficiency
differential.reasoning: Advanced CKD commonly leads to decreased erythropoietin production, explaining the observed anemia.

differential.name: Advanced Alzheimer’s disease with severe frailty and social isolation

supporting_evidence.finding: Documented diagnosis of Alzheimer’s disease, MMSE <10
Severe functional dependence, limited social support

differential.reasoning: The patient’s cognitive status and frailty are well‑established, influencing overall prognosis and care needs.

differential.name: Possible super‑imposed non‑diabetic glomerulopathy (e.g., membranous nephropathy)

supporting_evidence.finding: Nephrotic‑range proteinuria in an elderly diabetic
Rapid rise in serum creatinine over past 3 months

differential.reasoning: While diabetic nephropathy explains most findings, the magnitude of proteinuria and rapid decline raise the possibility of an additional glomerular disease, warranting further evaluation.

primary_diagnosis: Diabetic nephropathy (stage 4 chronic kidney disease with nephrotic-range proteinuria)
clinical_reasoning_summary: The patient’s advanced diabetic kidney disease, evidenced by stage 4 CKD and nephrotic‑range proteinuria, is the dominant pathology. Co‑existing atherosclerotic CAD with prior CABG, HFpEF, CKD‑related anemia, and severe Alzheimer’s disease each contribute to the clinical picture. A low‑probability consideration of a super‑imposed glomerulopathy remains given the unusually high protein loss and rapid renal decline. Congestive hepatopathy was excluded due to insufficient evidence.
unresolved_findings: Urine bilirubin 0.7 mg/dL – etiology unclear (congestive hepatopathy vs cholestasis vs medication effect)
Urine ketones 7 mg/dL – low‑grade ketonuria despite target HbA1c
Missing serum albumin, full liver panel, iron studies, lipid profile trend, blood pressure trend, medication list, BNP, echocardiogram, renal biopsy
recommended_workup: Serum albumin and total protein to assess hypoalbuminemia
Comprehensive liver panel (AST, ALT, ALP, GGT, bilirubin) to clarify bilirubin source
Iron studies (ferritin, transferrin saturation) and reticulocyte count for anemia work‑up
Lipid profile with trend over time
Review of current medication list for hepatotoxic or nephrotoxic agents
BNP or NT‑proBNP and transthoracic echocardiogram to confirm HFpEF and assess right‑sided pressures
Renal biopsy if proteinuria persists >5 g/day or if rapid renal decline continues, to rule out super‑imposed glomerulopathy
Abdominal ultrasound with Doppler to evaluate hepatic congestion vs biliary obstruction
